name: Washington
feeText: King County Superior Court Clerk: Dissolution of Marriage $364.00 (RCW 36.18.020(2),(5),(6); RCW 36.18.016(2)(b); RCW 36.18.016(15)). The statewide statutory part is $200 (RCW 36.18.020(2)(a)) + $40 surcharge (36.18.020(5)(c)) + $50 surcharge (36.18.020(6)) + $54 dissolution fee (36.18.016(2)(b)) = $344; counties may add up to $20 for a courthouse facilitator program (RCW 26.12.240).

otherFees.what: Counter Petition in a Domestic Relations Action (King County)
Statewide statutory base for a dissolution petition before county surcharges (RCW 36.18.020 + 36.18.016(2)(b))

waiver.name: Motion and Declaration for Waiver of Civil Fees and Surcharges (WPF GR 34.0100) with Order Re Waiver (WPF GR 34.0500)

residency.text: No minimum residence period: the petitioner must be a resident of Washington, a member of the armed forces stationed in Washington, or married to such a person (RCW 26.09.030).

waitingPeriod.text: The court may enter a decree only when ninety days have elapsed since the petition was filed and since service of the summons (or its first publication) on the respondent (RCW 26.09.030).

simplified.text: No separate summary dissolution procedure in chapter 26.09 RCW; agreed cases use the standard statewide divorce forms and the same 90-day wait.

parentingClass.text: No statewide statute requires a parenting class; some superior courts require a parenting seminar by local family law rule.

uncertain: Response fee: King County lists a $310 fee for a counter petition but no fee for a simple response; RCW 36.18.020(2)(a) charges only the first filer and parties filing a counterclaim, so responseFee is left null.
Parenting seminar: King County local family law rules (LFLR) were not read; requirement left null.
King County fee page carries no effective date; read on 2026-10-08.

name: Arizona
feeText: Maricopa County Clerk of Superior Court: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage with or without children $376.00; Response/Answer to Dissolution $287.00.

otherFees.what: Summary Consent Decree (with or without children), Maricopa County
Petition for Legal Separation, Maricopa County

waiver.name: Application for deferral or waiver of court fees and costs (A.R.S. 12-302; forms adopted by the Supreme Court)

residency.text: One spouse must have been domiciled in Arizona, or stationed there as a member of the armed services, for 90 days before filing (A.R.S. 25-312(A)(1)).

waitingPeriod.text: No trial, hearing or affidavit-based decree on a petition for dissolution or legal separation until 60 days after service or acceptance of process (A.R.S. 25-329).

simplified.text: Summary consent decree: spouses who agree on all issues can file jointly; Maricopa County charges $331.50 for a Summary Consent Decree (fee schedule). The 60-day wait of A.R.S. 25-329 still applies.

parentingClass.text: In a dissolution, legal separation or annulment involving a common minor child, the court shall order the parties to complete a domestic relations education program, unless the court finds it not in the best interests of the parties or child or a comparable program is completed (A.R.S. 25-352(A); programs under 25-351).

Eligibility conditions for a summary consent decree (Ariz. R. Fam. Law P.) were not read from the official rule text; only the fee and its existence are verified.
Exact title of the Supreme Court's fee deferral/waiver form not read (Maricopa waiver page blocked and not reachable in the archive at the time).

name: Massachusetts
feeText: Probate and Family Court: Divorce complaint (or joint petition) filing fee $200 plus $15 surcharge = $215.

otherFees.what: Motion in divorce actions during the nisi period
Complaint for modification of child support, custody or parenting time

residency.text: If the cause occurred outside Massachusetts, the plaintiff must have lived in the Commonwealth for one year before filing; if the cause occurred in Massachusetts, the plaintiff need only be domiciled there at filing, unless the plaintiff moved there to obtain a divorce (G.L. c. 208, § 5; see also § 4).

waitingPeriod.text: Joint petition (§ 1A): judgment nisi enters 30 days after the court approves the agreement, and becomes absolute 90 days later (§ 21), i.e. 120 days after approval. Contested no-fault complaint (§ 1B): no hearing earlier than six months after filing, then the 90-day nisi period.

simplified.text: Joint petition for divorce on irretrievable breakdown with a notarized separation agreement, no summons or answer required (G.L. c. 208, § 1A).

parentingClass.text: Not verified on an official page (Probate and Family Court parent education requirement).

uncertain: malegislature.gov refused connections on 2026-10-08; G.L. c. 208 §§ 1A, 1B, 4, 5 and 21 were read from Internet Archive copies (May-July 2026, § 4 Sept. 2025) of the official URLs.
mass.gov fee page read from the Internet Archive 2026 copy of the official URL (mass.gov returns 403/refuses automated clients). Fee for an answer not listed; responseFee null.
waitingPeriod.days = 120 counts from court approval of a § 1A agreement, not from filing; § 1B cases take at least 6 months + 90 days.
Affidavit of Indigency official page URL and the Probate and Family Court parent education requirement could not be read (mass.gov blocked, archive unavailable at the time).

name: Tennessee
feeText: Shelby County Circuit/Chancery Court clerk divorce filing fee not verified.

waiver.name: Request to Postpone Filing Fees and Order (Uniform Civil Affidavit of Indigency), Form 3 of the Supreme Court-approved divorce forms (Tenn. Sup. Ct. R. 29)

residency.text: The Supreme Court-approved agreed-divorce packet requires that one or both spouses lived in Tennessee for at least the past 6 months, or both lived in Tennessee when they decided to divorce (Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-4-104).

waitingPeriod.text: With minor children the soonest an irreconcilable-differences divorce can be granted is 90 days after filing (Supreme Court-approved forms instructions; Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-4-101). Without minor children the period is 60 days.

simplified.text: Supreme Court-approved agreed divorce forms for spouses who agree on everything and own no real property (with or without children).

parentingClass.text: All divorcing spouses with minor children must attend a parent education class unless the court excuses them (Supreme Court-approved forms instructions; Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-6-408).

uncertain: Shelby County filing fee not verified: shelbycountytn.gov court clerk sites return 403 and the Internet Archive was unavailable when tried.

Tennessee Code Annotated is published only through LexisNexis; statute sections are cited from the Supreme Court-approved forms instructions (read from the Internet Archive copy of tncourts.gov dated 2026-04-20, since tncourts.gov serves a browser-validation page to automated clients). The 60-day period without children was not read on an official page (the no-children packet PDF could not be downloaded).
waitingPeriod.days = 90 applies to cases with minor children.

name: Nebraska
feeText: District court Dissolution fee total $200.00 (mediation fee $50 and child abuse prevention fee $25 under § 33-106.03, docket fee § 33-106, plus the statutory add-on fees), schedule effective 07-01-2026.

otherFees.what: Proceeding to modify a decree of dissolution (legal services + mediation fees)

waiver.name: Affidavit and Application to Proceed Without Payment of Fees (In Forma Pauperis) DC 6:7.1, and Order to Proceed In Forma Pauperis DC 6:7.2

residency.text: At least one spouse must have actually resided in Nebraska with intent to make it a permanent home for at least one year before filing, unless the marriage was solemnized in Nebraska and a spouse has lived there since (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 42-349).

waitingPeriod.text: No divorce suit may be heard or tried until sixty days after perfection of service of process (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 42-363).

simplified.text: No summary procedure in statute; the Supreme Court publishes self-help divorce packets (no children; children without disputes).

parentingClass.text: The court shall order all parties to a proceeding under the Parenting Act to attend a basic level parenting education course, which may be delayed or waived for good cause (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 43-2928(1)).
